transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*bursts through the door, face flushed with indignation*

Severus! My crystallized pineapple is ruined — that jar was a gift from the Minister himself! And you've used my personal cauldron without asking! I have the Potions Guild inspection in two hours and the storeroom looks like a hippogriff went through it. You promised to keep it tidy!

*gestures wildly at the mess around the room*

What on earth have you been doing in here? This is absolutely unacceptable!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I assure you, I've been tidying up. It seems my efforts were somewhat... counterproductive. As for the crystallized pineapple, I must have mistaken it for a common leeching root. As for your cauldron, it was necessary for a crucial experiment. I did not anticipate returning so early from the summer break. I will clean this mess and locate a suitable replacement for the pineapple. There is no need to raise your voice, Slughorn. It is unbecoming.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face turning an even deeper shade of red*

Unbecoming? UNBECOMING?! Severus, you mistook crystallized pineapple for leeching root? They look nothing alike! One is golden and sugared, the other is — well, it's a root! Were you even paying attention?

*picks up the ruined jar, holding it up*

And "counterproductive tidying" is a contradiction in terms! The inspection committee will be here in TWO HOURS, and you think you can simply waltz down to Honeydukes and replace a gift from Cornelius Fudge himself? These were specially imported from the Caribbean!

*paces anxiously*

A "crucial experiment" — in MY personal cauldron? The pewter one with the brass handles that I've had since my days at Hogwarts? You have a dozen school cauldrons at your disposal! What could possibly have been so crucial that it couldn't wait, or use standard equipment?

*wringing his hands*

This is exactly why I was hesitant about letting you work in here unsupervised over the summer! You assured me you'd be meticulous!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Slughorn, I was addressing the situation with due haste. The pineapple was, clearly, an honest mistake. As for your cauldron, it was essential for a complex distillation process. Standard cauldrons lack the necessary precision. I did not anticipate the return of the inspection committee so soon. However, I will make amends. I will visit Honeydukes myself and secure a replacement. If they do not have an exact match, I will contact the head office in Diagon Alley. This is not a matter of triviality, but of expediency and practicality. Your cauldron will be returned to its proper state by the time the inspection begins.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*throws hands up in exasperation*

Expediency? EXPEDIENCY?! Severus, you're missing the point entirely! This isn't about whether you can rush about trying to fix things at the last minute — it's about respect! Respect for other people's belongings, respect for agreements we made!

*picks up a broken stirring rod from the floor*

And what's this? My dragon-bone stirring rod — snapped clean in half! These things don't grow on trees, you know. Dragon bone! Do you have any idea how expensive these are?

*mopping his brow with a handkerchief*

A "complex distillation process" — well, I'm sure it was fascinating, but that doesn't give you carte blanche to ransack my personal equipment! And you still haven't explained what this mysterious experiment was that couldn't possibly wait until term started, or use the perfectly adequate cauldrons in the main storage!

*looks around frantically*

The Guild inspectors are notoriously particular. Agatha Timbleweed once failed an entire academy because she found a single mislabeled ingredient! And you expect me to present a storeroom that looks like it's been hit by a Blasting Curse?

What exactly were you brewing that was so urgent?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: The experiment... involved the extraction of a highly volatile essence from a rare Amazonian root. It required precise temperature control and a cauldron with a thick base to prevent overheating. I could not risk using the cheaper, less reliable cauldrons in storage. As for the timing, the root loses its efficacy after three days in a warm environment. It was a narrow window of opportunity. I apologize for the... collateral damage. I will replace the stirring rod and菠萝罐头immediately. The storeroom will be restored to order by the time the inspectors arrive. There is no need for further... histrionics.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*eyes bulging*

Histrionics?! HISTRIONICS?! 

*clutches at his waistcoat dramatically*

I am NOT being histrionic, Severus! I am being justifiably upset! You've destroyed irreplaceable items, made unauthorized use of my personal property, and now you have the audacity to dismiss my entirely reasonable concerns as... as theatrics!

*waving the handkerchief about*

An Amazonian root! Well, that's all very impressive and exotic, I'm sure, but why wasn't I informed? If you had a rare specimen requiring immediate attention, the professional courtesy would have been to send an owl! I could have returned early, supervised the process, ensured my belongings remained intact!

*picks up a scattered pile of ingredient labels*

And you still think you can fix all this in two hours? Severus, I've seen you work, and yes, you're meticulous when it suits you, but this... this is beyond even your capabilities! The floor is sticky with something unidentifiable, there are stains on my best workbench, and half my inventory appears to have been moved about!

*voice rising to a near squeak*

What am I supposed to tell Agatha Timbleweed when she asks why everything is in chaos? "Oh, terribly sorry, Severus was extracting essences?" She'll have my certification suspended!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *mutters under breath* 'Professional courtesy'... as if you would have allowed the experiment to proceed under your... less than watchful eye. * aloud* The situation will be rectified. I am well-versed in the Guild's standards. Your certification will not be in jeopardy. As for the conversation with Timbleweed, I suggest a simple, "There was an... unexpected turn in a teaching exercise," followed by a strategic shift in the subject. The inspectors are more concerned with their own standing than that of the staff they're evaluating. I will clean the floor, reorder the shelves, and prepare the inventory. You will... focus on your presentation. We will ensure the storeroom is pristine. There is no need for further... melodrama.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face turning almost purple*

Melodrama?! MELODRAMA?! And what was that you just muttered? "Less than watchful eye?" I'll have you know I've been brewing potions since before you were BORN, young man! I taught you half of what you know!

*jabbing a finger in Severus's direction*

And don't you dare try to manipulate me with your little psychological games! "Strategic shift in the subject" — you mean LIE to Agatha Timbleweed? Mislead the Guild inspectors? Oh, that's rich coming from you! If she discovers we've been dishonest, it won't just be my certification on the line, it'll be the entire school's reputation!

*pacing more frantically now*

"Focus on my presentation" — as if I can waltz in there and charm them while wondering if you've actually managed to remove whatever sticky substance that is from the flagstones! What IS that, anyway? It smells faintly of... sulfur and treacle?

*stops and stares at him*

And another thing — you still haven't apologized! Not properly! You've said you'll fix things, you've made excuses about rare roots and narrow windows, but you haven't once said "I'm sorry, Horace, I overstepped badly and I understand why you're upset!"

Do you even comprehend how much stress this is causing me?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Very well, Horace. I apologize for the... mishandling of your possessions and the... untidiness of the storeroom. It was... unwise to proceed without your knowledge. The substance on the floor is a byproduct of the extraction process. It will be cleaned. As for the inspectors, I suggest we emphasize the... educational aspect of the experiment. They favor practical applications over mere theory. The storeroom will be in impeccable condition by the time they arrive. I assure you, there will be no... surprises. Now, if you will excuse me, I must begin the... rectification process.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*still looking flustered but slightly mollified*

Well... well, that's... that's more like it, I suppose. Though it did sound rather like you were pulling teeth there, Severus. A proper apology shouldn't require such... such evident effort.

*sighs heavily and dabs at his forehead*

Educational aspect... yes, I suppose we could frame it that way. Timbleweed does have a soft spot for innovative teaching methods. But Severus, if there's even a HINT of that sulfur-treacle substance remaining, or if a single jar is out of alphabetical order...

*looks around anxiously*

And what about my cauldron? Is it at least undamaged? Please tell me you didn't warp the base or scratch the interior coating. That cauldron has brewed some of the finest potions in Britain!

*wringing his hands again*

Two hours, Severus. Two hours! I need to change into my formal robes, prepare my notes, and calm my nerves — which, I might add, are completely frayed at this point! You're absolutely certain you can restore order in time?

*eyes him suspiciously*

And this Amazonian root experiment — it's... finished, isn't it? You're not going to need any MORE of my equipment?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: The cauldron is undamaged. The experiment is complete. I will restore order, and the storeroom will be ready for inspection. As for your equipment, I will return it to you in its original condition. There is no need for further... discussion. I suggest you attend to your personal preparations. I will handle the rest. Your... frazzled state is unbecoming of a Hogwarts professor. Calm yourself; the inspection will proceed as it should.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*bristles at the comment*

Unbecoming?! There you go AGAIN with the "unbecoming!" My state is perfectly reasonable given the circumstances! You don't get to create a disaster and then criticize me for being upset about it!

*huffs indignantly*

And I am NOT leaving you alone in here again — that's what got us into this mess in the first place! I'll change quickly and come straight back. I want to supervise this "restoration" of yours. Make sure you're actually putting things back properly and not just... just shoving everything into corners where Agatha won't immediately see!

*starts toward the door, then turns back sharply*

The pineapple, Severus! You said you'd replace it. Even if you apparate directly to Honeydukes, you'll need at least thirty minutes. And if they don't have the Caribbean variety, you absolutely MUST contact the importers. The Minister will ask about it when I see him at the next Ministry function, and I cannot — I will NOT — tell Cornelius Fudge that his thoughtful gift ended up in one of your experiments!

*voice becoming shrill again*

How do I know you won't just... vanish into your dungeon and leave me to face the inspectors alone with a half-cleaned storeroom?!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You have my word, Slughorn. The pineapple will be replaced. The storeroom will be restored. I will not... vanish. Your supervision is unnecessary, but if it reassures you, then by all means, stay. I will not miss your... constant surveillance. Now, if you will excuse me, I must begin the... aforementioned rectification process. I suggest you focus on your own... presentation. The inspectors will be here soon, and your... frazzled state will not inspire confidence in the quality of our instruction.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*sputtering with renewed indignation*

Constant surveillance?! It's MY storeroom, Severus! MINE! I have every right to supervise what happens in it, especially after what you've done!

*clutches his chest dramatically*

And stop telling me to focus on my presentation! How can I possibly focus when I'm worried you'll use some cleaning charm that leaves residue, or organize the shelves in that peculiar system of yours that nobody else can understand?

*takes a shaky breath*

Fine! FINE! I'll go change into my robes. But I'm giving you exactly twenty minutes, and then I'm coming back to check on your progress. Twenty minutes, Severus! And if I return to find you've made things WORSE somehow, or if that pineapple isn't en route from Honeydukes...

*wagging his finger*

You may think me fussy and theatrical, but at least I don't treat other people's property like disposable ingredients! At least I have the courtesy to ASK before I borrow things!

*moves toward the door, still muttering*

Unbecoming... frazzled... constant surveillance... I'll show YOU frazzled when Agatha Timbleweed walks in here and sees...

*trails off, still grumbling as he exits*

Twenty minutes, Severus! I'm timing you!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *nods in acknowledgment, still in character as Severus Snape*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*pauses at the doorway, turning back one more time*

And Severus? That sulfur-treacle mess better be GONE! Completely gone! Not just... masked with a Scouring Charm that'll wear off in an hour!

*points emphatically at the floor*

I want to see those flagstones gleaming! The same condition they were in when I left for summer! And the inventory list — it needs to match EXACTLY what's actually on the shelves. Agatha checks these things, you know. She's like a bloodhound for discrepancies!

*voice cracking slightly with stress*

Oh, this is a nightmare! An absolute nightmare! The one summer I decide to visit my old friend Eldred in Cornwall, and you turn my storeroom into... into some sort of experimental laboratory!

*pulls out a pocket watch*

Right. Twenty minutes. Starting... NOW!

*hurries out, still muttering about crystallized pineapple and dragon-bone stirring rods*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *nods again, adding a roll of the eyes in the direction of the door*

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*voice echoing from down the corridor*

I SAW THAT, SEVERUS! I know an eye-roll when I sense one! 

*footsteps pause*

And don't think I've forgotten about that cauldron! If there's even a SCRATCH on it, we'll be having words! WORDS, do you hear me?!

*footsteps resume, accompanied by continued muttering*

Amazonian roots... volatile essences... in MY cauldron... the absolute GALL of the man... twenty minutes... must find my ceremonial robes... where did I put that Guild medallion... oh, this is disastrous...

*voice fades as he hurries away*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *nods once more, then turns to address the storeroom with a mix of practicality and impatience*

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Engaged in complex experimental work with rare Amazonian root requiring precise distillation, showing intellectual curiosity and willingness to pursue novel potions research.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Used others' equipment without permission, created significant mess, mistook crystallized pineapple for leeching root, broke expensive dragon-bone stirring rod through carelessness.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Repeatedly dismissive of emotional expression, tells Slughorn to calm down and stop being histrionic, prefers to work alone without supervision or collaboration.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Dismisses Slughorn's legitimate concerns as 'melodrama' and 'histrionics,' gives grudging apology that 'sounded like pulling teeth,' subtly insults with 'less than watchful eye' comment.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Remains calm and composed throughout intense confrontation, responds with measured irritation rather than anxiety, maintains controlled demeanor despite accusations and anger directed at him.
